messages.content: "Can you help me plan a trip? I need to know the distance in kilometers from New York to London using the 'geodistance.find' function, then I want to know the time difference between New York and London using the 'timezones.get_difference' function. After that, I want to find flights from New York to London on the date of 'next friday' using the 'flights.search' function. Finally, I want to know the distance in miles from London to Paris using the 'geodistance.find' function again."

function.description: Find the distance between two cities on the globe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

2. Time difference between New York and London using timezones_get_difference.

3. Flights from New York to London on next Friday using flights_search.

The user didn't specify the date format for next Friday; we can pass date as "next friday". The geodistance_find function expects origin, destination, unit optional. For first call, unit: "kilometers". For last call, unit: "miles" (default). So we need to produce separate function calls. The user wants us to do them in order. We'll produce four calls. We can chain them: we can call the first function, get result, then call second, etc. But we can't produce multiple calls in one response. We need to produce them sequentially. So we will produce the first call. Then after receiving the result, we produce the second call, etc. But the user wants all four calls. We can produce them one after another. So we need to produce four separate responses. The user wants us to do them in order. So we produce the first call. Then we wait for the tool's response. Then we produce the second call. And so on.
